subject: Intermittent 5xxs & elevated tail latency — hosted token-queue pressure (KnoxHealth)
body:
From: Alyssa Gentry <alyssa@knoxhealth.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@knoxhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:51:22 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 500s and hung generations (examples attached)

Hi Soojin,

Starting around 07:40 PT we've seen a ~0.6% spike in failed generation requests (5xx) and several longer-than-expected response times for our nightly summarization jobs. Attach a small sample of request IDs and timestamps; stack traces in our logs point to timeouts on the generation call rather than our side.

This is impacting downstream data pipelines that expect sub-second inference for small batches (N=1-4). Can you confirm if there's an ongoing incident on your hosted API or routing for our tenant? If you need more traces we can share.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Gentry
Director, Platform Reliability — KnoxHealth

Attachment: request-ids.txt (text, 42 lines)

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the heads-up and the request IDs, they were very helpful. We’re investigating with priority.

Quick summary of what we’re doing now:
- I’ve opened an ops bridge and assigned the incident to Ben (serving/runtime) to triage kernel/runtime queueing and KV-cache contended paths.
- We’ve started real-time log collection for the request IDs you sent.
- I’ll keep you updated on mitigation steps and expected timeline.

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether the affected requests were predominantly short contexts (<=512 tokens) and high concurrency (many concurrent single-turn requests)? That pattern helps us reproduce.

We’ll send a status update within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we know even small error rates are disruptive when they hit critical jobs.

— Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:38:11 -0700
Subject: RE: Intermittent 500s and hung generations (examples attached)

Team — initial findings from runtime traces:
- Symptom: short-lived backlog on the tokenization/dispatch queue for hosted-inference workers serving the us-west region. This causes head-of-line blocking for subsequent requests and in ~0.5-0.8% of cases a request times out (we surface as 500).
- Trigger: a kernel scheduling regression introduced in the 2027-09-10 runtime patch interacts poorly with high-concurrency small-batch traffic and long-context prefix cache invalidation. The root cause appears to be a mutex handoff delay inside the tokenizer/kv-cache path under specific task-switch patterns.

Actions taken (immediate):
1) Applied a runtime config change to increase the tokenizer worker thread pool for the affected pool (reduces queue growth).
2) Temporarily routed KnoxHealth traffic to an alternate capacity pool in a neighboring AZ that does not show the same lock contention pattern.
3) Increased autoscaling headroom for KnoxHealth’s tenant pool by 15% while we validate the hotfix.

Planned (short window):
- Rolling hotfix (revert of the scheduling regression + targeted mutex fix) scheduled for 2027-09-14 11:00 PT. This is low-risk; we’ll do canary rollout and watch tail latencies.
- Post-deploy verification for 90 minutes across representative traffic shapes.

User-facing impact so far: reduced error rate from ~0.6% to ~0.1% for routed traffic; tail latency improved but we will confirm across all regions after the hotfix.

I’ll post a runbook-style update to the incident page and attach a short timeline once the hotfix completes.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Subject: Hosted API incident update — tokenization queue pressure (KnoxHealth)

Hi Alyssa / Knox Ops —

Thanks again for the report and the logs. Quick customer-facing summary and current status:

What happened
- Between ~07:40–09:00 PT we observed tokenization/dispatch queue pressure in the us-west serving fleet for a subset of small-batch, high-concurrency requests. The condition caused increased head-of-line blocking and a small fraction of timed-out requests (5xx).

What we did
- Immediately increased tokenizer worker threads for the affected pool and routed KnoxHealth traffic to a secondary capacity pool.
- Increased temporary autoscaling headroom for your tenant by 15% to absorb immediate load spikes.
- Performed a canary-deploy hotfix at 11:00 PT that reverts the scheduling regression and applies a targeted mutex handoff optimization. Canary metrics look good.

Current status
- Error rate for KnoxHealth requests linked to this issue has decreased from ~0.6% to ~0.05% for routed traffic. We will continue to monitor for 24 hours and complete a full verification run across representative job shapes.

What to expect next
- We’ll post a full incident timeline and postmortem on our status page and attach the runbook and timeline (link below).
- Offer: as this incident impacted critical pipelines, we’d like to offer a one-off service credit for 10% of this month’s hosted inference spend for KnoxHealth (we can discuss accounting/contract details).
- If helpful, we can schedule a short technical sync with Ben and Marissa to walk through the root cause and mitigation details. Please let me know two times that work.

Links & artifacts
- Incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/knoxhealth-token-queue-pressure-2027-09-14
- Internal ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/OPS-4897
- Postmortem draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b-token-queue-hotfix-plan

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (CSV, 1.2KB)

Again, sorry for the disruption. If you notice any further anomalies please flag them and we’ll prioritize.
